h1: Metal shears — hydraulic, mechanical and sheet metal shears, 20 ga to 1-9/16″
intro: A metal shear (sheet metal shearing machine, guillotine shear, shear cutter) cuts plate and sheet to size in one stroke between a fixed bottom blade and a top blade on the moving beam — the first machine in every sheet-metal, HVAC, signage and fabrication shop, before the press brake. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic shears — swing beam and variable-rake guillotine plate shears from 12 ga to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft, in a premium line made in Turkey and a value line built to our specification; mechanical guillotine shears — direct-gear SRGM machines for 1/8″ and 1/4″ at 31 to 35 strokes a minute and flywheel shears to 3/8″, with no hydraulics at all; and sheet metal shears — pneumatic, electric and bench shears and a coil slitter for the sheet-metal shop. Below, the three kinds compared, every model in one table of capacity, length, strokes, motor and weight, and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Hydraulic, mechanical or sheet metal shear — which should I buy?
faq.a: By the material and the hours. For sheet to 14 ga in a sheet-metal, HVAC or signage shop, the sheet metal shears are the lowest-priced powered machines — pneumatic, electric or bench, 26″ to 100″. For 1/8″ and 1/4″ all day, a mechanical guillotine shear is the faster and simpler machine: direct-gear drive, 31 – 35 strokes a minute, no hydraulics, with return-to-sender and cut-to-length versions. From 1/4″ plate up — 3/8″, 1/2″, to 1-9/16″ over 20 and 26 ft — the hydraulic shears are the machines, swing beam for the everyday plate shear and a variable-rake guillotine for production and thick plate; each comes in a premium and a value line on the same page. Every kind is installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.

The premium hydraulic shears (Dener BS / BSY and DAS CNC) and mechanical shears (SRGM) are built in Turkey on the heaviest frames with European hydraulics, motors and controls and parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — for two shifts a day and the tightest cut. NovoTech's value line — the QC12K / Q11K hydraulic shears with Estun controls and the sheet metal shears — is built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price, the right buy for a job shop. Both lines are sections on the hydraulic shear page, so the comparison is side by side.

faq.q: Mechanical or hydraulic shear — which is better?
faq.a: For sheet to 1/4″ a mechanical shear is the faster and simpler machine: 30 – 55 strokes a minute from a motor and gearbox or flywheel, no hydraulic power pack, no oil to heat up, no valves or seals to service, and the same cut quality on the first and the thousandth stroke. Hydraulic shears earn their price from 3/8″ plate upwards, where the beam needs tonnage rather than speed — and in the light sizes a small hydraulic shear is the quietest, lowest-priced way to cut 14 ga to 5/32″ a few times an hour.

On a swing beam shear the beam pivots on two bearings and the cylinders swing it through the cut — few parts, a low price and a rake angle fixed by the design, which is fine for plate. A guillotine shear carries the beam straight down on rollers with a variable rake angle, so the same machine cuts thin sheet flat and fast at a small angle and thick plate at a steeper one; it also keeps the blade gap set automatically. For a plate shop cutting mostly 3/8″ and up, a swing beam shear (Dener BS, NovoTech QC12K); for a job shop that cuts everything from 16 ga to 3/4″ and beyond, a guillotine (Dener DAS, NovoTech Q11K).

faq.q: How is the capacity rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: Capacities are the makers' ratings for mild steel (about 65,000 psi) over the full blade length. Stainless steel is harder to shear, so count on about 60 % of the mild-steel thickness — 14 ga stainless on a 1/8″ machine, 11 ga on a 1/4″ machine, 3/8″ on a 5/8″ machine; aluminum cuts to the full rated thickness and about 50 % more. Tell us your thickest material and we size the shear with a margin.

The model number is the maximum shearing length in millimetres: 1250 – 1360 = 49 – 53.5″ (a 4 × 8 sheet cut across), 1500 – 1560 = 5 ft, 2000 – 2060 = 6.6 – 6.8 ft, 2500 – 2560 = 8.2 – 8.4 ft (a 4 × 8 sheet lengthwise), 3000 – 3200 = 10 – 10.5 ft (5 × 10 sheet), 4000 = 13 ft, 6000 = 20 ft plate. Most sheet-metal shops run an 8 or 10 ft machine so a full sheet is cut both ways; HVAC and signage shops are well served by 52 – 81″; plate shops buy 10 to 20 ft.

faq.q: What is the back gauge, and is it NC?
faq.a: The back gauge is the stop behind the blade that sets the width of the cut strip. The value-line sheet metal shears have a manual gauge with counter, an electric gauge or a PLC-positioned gauge depending on the model; the SRGM and the hydraulic plate shears come with an NC back gauge — the operator keys in the dimension and the gauge moves there — and the Dener DAS with a 1 m ball-screw gauge set by the CNC together with the blade gap and the cutting angle.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Finger guards along the blade, rear guard fences or photocells / light curtains, an anti-repeat single-stroke control and a mobile foot pedal with emergency stop are standard or available on every line; we recommend the photocell or light-curtain rear guard on every powered shear. In Ontario a new shear needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs; NovoTech prepares the documentation for it.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — every shear is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled, commissioned and the operators trained by NovoTech; blades and parts for all four lines are stocked here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request) and a 1-year warranty.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
